capture.final_message:
Treat each equivalence as relating two independently true trigonometric facts.

- For the first equivalence, prove complex sine’s \(2\pi\)-periodicity from the sine subtraction formula, using
  \[
  \sin(2\pi)=0,\qquad \cos(2\pi)=1
  \]
  after embedding \(\mathbb R\) into \(\mathbb C\). Prove injectivity of real tangent on \((-\pi/2,\pi/2)\) using its strict monotonicity there. Thus both sides hold, yielding the equivalence.

- For the second equivalence, establish the natural-number shift formula by induction from
  \[
  \sin(t-\pi)=-\sin t.
  \]
  The integer statement immediately specializes to naturals. Conversely, split an integer into the nonnegative and negative cases. For \(n=-m\), derive the positive-shift identity
  \[
  \sin(x+m\pi)=(-1)^m\sin x
  \]
  by applying the natural-number formula to \(x+m\pi\); also use that \((-1)^{-m}=(-1)^m\). This extends the formula from \(\mathbb N\) to all of \(\mathbb Z\).
